draft.title: Trends in the periodic table
card: Metals sit on the left and in the middle of the periodic table. Non-metals sit on the right. A staircase line separates them.
Across a period, from left to right, atoms get smaller. More protons pull the outer electrons in more strongly, but no new shell is added.
Down a group, atoms get larger. Each element has one more electron shell than the one above it, so the outer electrons sit further from the nucleus.
In group 1, reactivity rises down the group. The outer electron is further from the nucleus and held less tightly, so it is lost more easily. Potassium reacts more strongly with water than lithium.
draft.remember: Atoms shrink across a period and grow down a group. Group 1 metals get more reactive going down.

a.q: Sodium and chlorine are in the same period. Sodium is on the left and chlorine is on the right. Which statement is correct?
opts: A chlorine atom is smaller than a sodium atom
A chlorine atom is larger than a sodium atom
A chlorine atom has more shells than a sodium atom
A chlorine atom has fewer protons than a sodium atom
a.why: Atoms get smaller across a period, so chlorine, further right, is smaller than sodium. The shell count stays the same across a period, so more shells is wrong. More protons pull the outer electrons in more strongly.
a.clue: Both elements are in the same row, so think about what changes across a period.

b.q: Rubidium is below potassium in group 1. Why is rubidium expected to react more strongly with water than potassium?
opts: Its outer electron is further out and is lost more easily
Its outer electron is closer in and is lost more easily
Its atom is smaller, so the outer electron is held loosely
Its atom has the same shells, so it loses electrons faster
b.why: Going down a group, atoms have more shells, so the outer electron sits further from the nucleus and is held less tightly. That makes it easier to lose, so reactivity rises. The idea that the atom is smaller is the wrong direction, because atoms get larger down a group.
b.clue: Think about how the size of the atom changes down a group.

a.best: A chlorine atom is smaller than a sodium atom

b.best: Its outer electron is further out and is lost more easily
